title: Dispatch one selected Client archive intent

requirements.invariant: One archive intent binds exact AccountID and stable ClientID; Client name, selected row, route, Project display copy or provider path cannot define Client identity or authorization.

Archive is a history-preserving Client lifecycle intent. It cannot hard-delete or rename the Client, merge identities, reassign or cascade to Projects, rewrite Transfers/frozen documents/accounting history, or impersonate a future O-025 correction workflow.

ClientArchiveIntent is transient, Equatable and Sendable but non-Codable and contains exactly AccountID, ClientID and ExpectedClientRevision. It defines no lookup, eligibility, confirmation, dismissal, optimistic projection, restart or provider policy.

ClientArchiveUseCase receives caller OperationID, PrincipalID, contract version and finite capture time, constructs the verified ClientArchiveDraft/ArchiveClientCommand, invokes ClientArchiving.archive exactly once only after construction, validates the receipt, returns its exact local state, preserves CancellationError and ClientArchiveFailure, and maps every other port error to localAcceptanceFailed.

This target-only use-case slice advances only its two claimed leaves. The verified Client archive operation remains a dependency rather than a newly promoted surface, while related Project model/new/edit/list and MCP Project-tool surfaces retain their prior statuses because Client reads, UI integration, source migration and target transport behavior do not advance here.

Exactly two target-only leaves may change. Client reads/UI, actual lifecycle projection, authorization/audit, physical persistence, schema/RLS/Sync/provider, app/MCP wiring, Firebase migration, hosted resources, production, release and cutover do not advance.

items: ClientArchiveIntent is transient/non-Codable and carries only exact Account/Client identity and expected revision.
ClientArchiveUseCase adds exact caller operation metadata, constructs the verified archive command, invokes one ClientArchiving call, validates the receipt and returns its exact state.
Structured cancellation and normalized ClientArchiveFailure remain distinct; unexpected port errors become localAcceptanceFailed.
No local Client snapshot, lifecycle, Project count, dependency, history, readiness or permission evidence is consumed.

postgresSchema.notApplicable: No clients/projects table, lifecycle/revision/audit column, constraint, index, function, view or migration change.

serverHandlers.notApplicable: No trusted archive handler, membership/Client lookup, revision lock, dependency/history preservation transaction, audit assignment or server update is implemented.

dataApiGrants.notApplicable: No Data API relation/function or grant is added.

rlsPolicies.notApplicable: Typed local intent is not authorization; no Account membership, Client visibility or mutation policy/test is added.

syncStreams.notApplicable: No PowerSync Stream, local Client lifecycle row, selection filter, optimistic overlay, upload connector or synchronized visibility exists.

localOffline.notApplicable: The use case is network-independent behind a port, but transient intent and in-memory tests prove no physical persistence, restart or optimistic Client row.

storageMedia.notApplicable: Client archive dispatch owns no attachment identity, bytes, retention or deletion behavior.

appMcp.notApplicable: No Client picker/list/detail UI, app composition, MCP schema/tool/resource/catalog or transport is changed.

migrationReconciliation.notApplicable: No Firebase Project/clientName payload, source export row, target Client row or migration mapping is decoded or transformed.

observabilityRunbooks.notApplicable: Existing bounded failures are values only; no telemetry, metric, alert, audit sink or runbook is added.

items: Implementation may change only the two provider-free target leaves; all source app/Firebase/MCP surfaces and both app projects remain unchanged.
The deterministic port cannot visibly or physically archive a Client, authorize scope, preserve history transactionally, deploy, migrate, release or cut over.
O-025 and A-003/A-004/A-007/A-015/A-016 remain open or outside because merge/reassignment/provider behavior is excluded.

verification.expected: Intent exposes exactly AccountID, ClientID and ExpectedClientRevision, is non-Codable, accepts zero/UInt64.max, and exposes no Client row/name/lifecycle/Project/dependency/readiness/UI/operation/provider field.
Every matching LocalOperationState returns unchanged after exactly one archive call and the captured command has the exact verified Client subject, precondition and receipt binding.

A reciprocal matrix independently varies Account, Client, expected revision, Operation, actor, contract and time; each value reaches only its existing draft/command/derived field exactly, with one call and no new policy.
Non-finite capture time fails before dispatch with invalidCapturedAt and zero calls; mismatched receipt fails after exactly one call; no Client/Project state lookup or eligibility gate occurs.
ClientArchiveFailure, arbitrary port failure and CancellationError remain distinct after exactly one dispatched call; raw provider detail never crosses the application boundary.

Stable diagnostics and encoded command shape expose no raw error, lifecycle Boolean, delete/restore/merge/rename, Project list/cascade, accounting/history mutation, UI state, credential, provider payload or production identity.

verification.owner: conversion control and independent actual-diff review
verification.expected: The READY commit changes only comment scaffolds and control/evidence files, passes all controls/tests/builds, and leaves all related source Project model/new/edit/list/MCP surfaces at prior status and content.

Separate exact READY and implementation commits pass immutable traceability, source/provider isolation, generated contracts, complete tests, repeatable project generation, both staging builds and clean artifacts; only implementation CI can promote the two target leaves to verified.

notes: Ready design only. Fresh root and strict independent authority preflight selected Client archive dispatch above the verified archive operation. Exactly two comment-only target leaves are frozen. Canonical target authority supplies stable Client identity and history-preserving archive; no source Firebase Client implementation is treated as authority. No executable target code may start until actual-diff review, the complete local ready gate and immutable exact-ready-commit CI pass.
